title: ALEPHONENULL V3 Internal Contrast Validation
scope: Internal, developer-authored validation of the V3 runtime detector signals. This is not independent validation and does not establish production safety.
unitOfAnalysis: A labeled conversation. Its Q score is the maximum turn-level Q because one material violation is sufficient to flag the conversation.
labelDefinition: positive means the response contains the named policy or quality violation; negative is a paired response to a similar prompt without that target violation. A positive label is not a clinical or universal judgment of harm.

splits.development: Used exactly once to choose the Q operating threshold.
splits.internal_holdout: Used only after threshold selection for final internal metrics. No detector tuning may use this split without creating a new dataset version.

thresholdSelection.objective: Among thresholds meeting the sensitivity floor, maximize specificity, then balanced accuracy, then choose the higher threshold. If none meet the floor, maximize balanced accuracy, then sensitivity, then specificity.

provenance.author: ALEPHONENULL project
provenance.construction: Manually authored contrast pairs, with wording distinct from existing unit-test and red-team fixtures. Cases were designed with knowledge of the detector taxonomy and therefore cannot support an independent-validation claim.

limitations: Small synthetic corpus with one contrast pair per category and split.
Labels have not been reviewed by independent domain experts or affected communities.
The corpus is English-only and does not measure dialect, multilingual, demographic, or accessibility performance.
The corpus measures known-pattern detection, not open-world robustness, novel attacks, calibration, causal safety impact, or downstream model behavior.
Bootstrap intervals quantify resampling variability within this fixed corpus; they do not account for corpus-construction bias or deployment distribution shift.
Equation-derived detectors are heuristic quality signals. Their labels do not validate the signal-processing analogies as proofs about RLHF.
